title: WHO CONTROLS TATA SONS? Harish Salve On Board, Trusts, Chandra & RBI | Tata Sons vs Tata Company

title_detail.value: WHO CONTROLS TATA SONS? Harish Salve On Board, Trusts, Chandra & RBI | Tata Sons vs Tata Company

summary: The Tata Sons–Tata Trusts governance dispute takes a fresh legal turn as senior lawyer Harish Salve speaks exclusively to Rahul Shivshankar on the questions surrounding the Tata Sons board, N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment and the company’s proposed listing. The Tata Sons board has approved a fresh five-year term for Chandrasekaran by majority vote, while Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata opposed the resolution and the Trusts have called the decision a “legal nullity.” At the heart of the dispute is the role of Tata Trusts’ nominee directors, the company’s Articles of Association and whether a chairman’s casting vote can resolve a disagreement involving the Trusts’ nominees. summary: A shocking price gap in hospital consumables has come under the Maharashtra FDA’s scanner, with one IV infusion set reportedly carrying an MRP nearly 28 times its trade procurement price.Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe highlighted findings from a survey examining the prices of commonly used medical consumables. According to the figures cited, an IV infusion set purchased at a trade price of ₹11.05 carried a printed MRP of ₹325, which is a difference of around 28 times, or a reported 2,841% markup. The survey also found major gaps in several other products.Mundhe said patients undergoing hospital treatment often have little opportunity to compare prices or question the cost of individual consumables while receiving care.
